column1: # The checks of shell/devdb-setup.nsh, the Shell boot of shell-devdb-setup, in Setup Mode. See
# uefisettings refuses the append before SetVariable(), which may write devdb unverified in Setup
# Mode (UEFI 2.11 section 32.6.3), and devdb stays absent

column3: . == {"error_message": "EFI variable devdb-b9c2b4f4-bf5f-462d-8adf-c5c70ac35dad is a device signature database and SetupMode is 1, so the firmware may write it without checking the payload's signature (UEFI 2.11 section 32.6.3)"}

column1: # with the flag, the append creates devdb, which holds devdb.esl

column3: .variable == "devdb-b9c2b4f4-bf5f-462d-8adf-c5c70ac35dad" and .attributes == 39 and (.value | length) == 1 and .value[0].type == "A5C059A1-94E4-4AA7-87B5-AB155C2BF072" and (.value[0].signatures | length) == 1 and .value[0].signatures[0].owner == "8C78A505-BAA0-4C4A-869F-000000000400"

column1: # edk2 verifies devdb as a private authenticated variable, in Setup Mode too, and takes its
# updates only from the signer that created it (edk2-stable202508, which the i686 and aarch64
# secboot images build, and edk2-stable202608: AuthVariableLibProcessVariable routes devdb to
# ProcessVariable, and VerifyTimeBasedPayload checks it in its AuthVarTypePriv branch); x86_64's
# pinned image, ovmf 2024.02-2ubuntu0.10, has no source here, so this step alone shows it there.
# A firmware that writes devdb unverified, as section 32.6.3 lets it, fails other-signer.

column3: .variable == "devdb-b9c2b4f4-bf5f-462d-8adf-c5c70ac35dad" and .attributes == 39 and (.value | length) == 2 and all(.value[]; .type == "A5C059A1-94E4-4AA7-87B5-AB155C2BF072" and (.signatures | length) == 1 and .signatures[0].owner == "8C78A505-BAA0-4C4A-869F-000000000400") and .value[0].signatures[0].sha256 != .value[1].signatures[0].sha256
